items.prompt:
Biodiversity is:
A) The number of rocks in an area
B) The variety of living things in an ecosystem
C) The amount of water
D) The temperature
items.answer: B) The variety of living things in an ecosystem

steps: Biodiversity is the variety of life in an ecosystem.

items.prompt:
Which is an example of an ecosystem service?
A) Pollination of crops
B) A video game
C) A parking lot
D) A traffic light

steps: Pollination is a benefit ecosystems provide.

items.prompt:
Which action helps protect biodiversity?
A) Paving over a wetland
B) Creating a nature preserve
C) Removing all plants
D) Draining a lake

steps: A nature preserve protects habitat and species.

items.prompt:
Why does losing bees threaten food production?
A) Bees eat crops
B) Bees pollinate many food plants
C) Bees make soil
D) Bees cause droughts
items.answer: B) Bees pollinate many food plants

steps: Bees pollinate crops, an ecosystem service food plants depend on.

items.prompt:
When scientists evaluate competing conservation plans, they mainly weigh:
A) Only the costs
B) The benefits and costs of each plan
C) The names of the plans
D) Nothing
items.answer: B) The benefits and costs of each plan

steps: Evaluating solutions means comparing their benefits and costs.

items.prompt:
Higher biodiversity often makes an ecosystem more stable because:
A) It has fewer species
B) A variety of species keeps functions going if one is lost
C) It removes all services
D) It stops energy flow
items.answer: B) A variety of species keeps functions going if one is lost

steps: Diverse species provide backups that keep the ecosystem working.

items.prompt:
A town chooses between a preserve and a parking lot on the same land. Which best supports an argument for the preserve?
A) It provides more parking
B) It maintains habitat and the ecosystem services the species provide
C) It removes biodiversity
D) It has no benefits
items.answer: B) It maintains habitat and the ecosystem services the species provide

steps: The preserve protects habitat and the services that depend on biodiversity.

items.prompt:
Why evaluate 'competing' solutions rather than adopting the first idea?
A) To waste time
B) Because each has different benefits and costs, and comparing finds the best balance
C) Because all solutions are identical
D) Because biodiversity does not matter
items.answer: B) Because each has different benefits and costs, and comparing finds the best balance

steps: Comparing trade-offs leads to a better-informed decision.
